entry.title: August payroll data show an uneven industrial employment picture
entry.summary: BLS reports a preliminary, seasonally adjusted gain of 16,000 U.S. manufacturing jobs and a decline of 23,000 information-sector jobs in August 2026. These broad sectors include activity beyond AI, so the changes cannot be attributed to AI alone.

entry.title: What the August jobs report establishes
entry.summary: BLS reports gains of 22,000 construction jobs and 8,000 nonresidential specialty trade jobs, a subset of construction. BLS calls overall construction little changed. These broad industry figures do not isolate electricians or AI projects.

entry.title: Reading the White House article
entry.summary: The administration presents the August report as evidence for its reindustrialization agenda. The ledger uses the underlying BLS release for measured payroll changes; those figures alone do not establish policy or AI causation.

entry.title: Stargate is tracked campus by campus
entry.summary: Epoch’s Abilene record distinguishes an estimated current IT footprint from its end-state projection. Stack Ledger now separates additional New Mexico, Wisconsin, Michigan, Ohio and Texas sites, preserving different construction and operating evidence instead of assigning the program envelope to every campus.

entry.title: Indiana HBM packaging gets a revised production schedule
entry.summary: SK hynix reports groundbreaking for its Indiana packaging and test facility. The updated release distinguishes cleanroom readiness from later mass production, moving beyond the older overview’s earlier operations target. Korean wafer fabrication and U.S. packaging remain separate production steps.

entry.title: The electrician outlook includes AI and the grid
entry.summary: BLS projects electrician employment to grow 9% over 2025–2035 and cites data centers, grid upgrades and renewable power connections among the drivers. Projected annual openings include replacement needs.

entry.title: Cape Station advances commissioning with a phased power schedule
entry.summary: Fervo reports mechanical completion on its first two GeoBlocks. Block 1 targets first power in Q4 2026, with blocks 2 and 3 following in early 2027; Phase II targets 2028. Commissioning progress should not be recorded as the entire first phase already generating.

entry.title: Actual electricity output is growing alongside capacity plans
entry.summary: EIA estimates U.S. electric power sector generation rose by 37 billion kWh, or 1.8%, in the first half of 2026 versus the same period in 2025. Solar and wind generation increased 21% and 6%. These are historical output changes, not nameplate additions or electricity dedicated to AI.

entry.title: Terafab enters the delivery ledger as a commitment
entry.summary: SpaceX identifies a Texas site and an initial investment requirement for Terafab. The ledger separates this future chip-manufacturing program from Tesla Cortex training compute and the Colossus data centers. Permits, first wafers and qualified production remain milestones to verify.

entry.title: Texas grid-connection review changes the scheduling context
entry.summary: ERCOT says data-center large loads must undergo verification before advancing through interconnection, and delays its planned Batch Zero classification notices. The notice does not establish that Abilene’s operating facilities have stopped or identify the effect on each expansion.

entry.title: Colossus power transition has a dated removal schedule
entry.summary: SpaceXAI reports a permanent Southaven power plant under construction and an agreed schedule for removing temporary turbines. Grid energization, temporary generation, the permitted future plant and the filed legal challenge are tracked separately. Actual removals and operating output require follow-up evidence.

entry.title: Tesla driving and robotics retain their deployment stages
entry.summary: Tesla’s shareholder update distinguishes consumer FSD supervision from city-specific Robotaxi operations. Optimus training builds and manufacturing preparations do not establish a productive deployed fleet. Cortex compute is tracked separately from driving exposure and physical work.

entry.title: TSMC and Amkor extend the Arizona packaging supply chain
entry.summary: The companies describe a long-term U.S. advanced-packaging partnership while Amkor’s Arizona campus and TSMC’s fabrication facilities continue development. An agreement and an expanding site do not establish commissioned packaging throughput.

entry.title: Hyperion’s expanded campus remains a construction-stage plan
entry.summary: Meta describes a 5 GW campus expansion and future Entergy-backed energy infrastructure. The project tracker keeps the announced rating separate from verified operational capacity and asks for generation, grid and data-center commissioning evidence.

entry.title: Hyperion separates local contracts from investment plans
entry.summary: Meta’s Richland Parish update distinguishes contracts awarded to Louisiana businesses from its regional investment plans and future staffing. The jobs table keeps expected peak construction work apart from promised permanent roles; contracts awarded are not labeled as cash already paid.

entry.title: Grid agreements are improving, but the queue is not delivered power
entry.summary: Berkeley Lab reports 2,061 GW of generation and storage active in end-2025 queues. Several regions processed record agreement volumes, while the median path to commercial operation exceeded five years in the available regional data. Queue withdrawals also contributed to the smaller backlog.

entry.title: Memory capacity outlook points to further expansion
entry.summary: SEMI projects global 300mm memory fabrication capacity of 4.1 million wafers per month in 2026 and 4.2 million in 2027. These are forecasts covering memory broadly, not HBM-only output or accelerator shipments.

entry.title: Fairwater moves from construction plans to reported operation
entry.summary: Microsoft reports its first Mount Pleasant facility fully operational, with nearly 550 full-time employees on site. Construction of the adjacent second facility continues toward a 2028 completion schedule. No commissioned-MW total is supplied in this release.

entry.title: CHPE adds an operating transmission link to New York City
entry.summary: The developer reports commercial operation and power deliveries on the 1,250 MW Quebec-to-New York City link. This is transmission capability, not new generating capacity. The June disclosure also identifies temporary market restrictions; later resolution remains a follow-up.

entry.title: Qcells starts U.S. solar cell manufacturing
entry.summary: Qcells reported starting Cartersville solar cell production in June 2026, with module assembly at full capacity. Full integrated production remained targeted for Q3, and the combined Georgia workforce figure was an expectation, not verified hiring.

entry.title: Model capability needs a reliability threshold
entry.summary: METR’s current Time Horizon 1.1 page distinguishes 50% and 80% success on software tasks measured in human-expert time. It warns that measurements above 16 hours are unreliable with its current task suite. These results do not establish dependable autonomy across ordinary jobs.

entry.title: Waymo operating service has a measurable footprint
entry.summary: Alphabet reports fully autonomous rides across an expanded U.S. service footprint. The ledger keeps this disclosure separate from Waymo’s older explicitly paid-trip run-rate, commercial vehicle count and rider-only safety mileage, retaining each record’s geography and date.

entry.title: A clearer view of the power ahead
entry.summary: The IEA’s updated outlook puts global data-center electricity consumption at roughly 950 TWh in 2030, from 485 TWh in 2025. Grid delivery and equipment supply remain important to realizing that growth.

entry.title: New inference results broaden the measurement toolkit
entry.summary: MLPerf Inference v6.0 adds a GPT-OSS 120B workload and an interactive DeepSeek-R1 scenario permitting speculative decoding. Compare compatible workloads, quality targets, accelerator counts and serving scenarios. Throughput results do not by themselves measure dollar cost or application reliability.

entry.title: Inference price-performance research extends the cost picture
entry.summary: A revised research paper estimates roughly 5–10-fold annual declines in the price of achieving a fixed benchmark performance level across several task families. This is a retrospective benchmark-based estimate, not a guarantee that frontier API prices or every real task get cheaper at that rate.

entry.title: Coherent optical engines · demonstration announced
entry.summary: Coherent announced OFC demonstrations of several CPO architectures and components. This is a demonstration announcement, not evidence of installed production capacity.

entry.title: A longer horizon for firm power
entry.summary: DOE describes a 400 GW U.S. nuclear capacity goal for 2050. It is an economy-wide ambition; tracking operational additions will help distinguish the target from delivered power.

entry.title: Lightmatter Passage · sampling reported
entry.summary: Lightmatter reported Passage chiplet sampling and a throughput demonstration. Sampling is earlier than volume deployment.

entry.title: Samsung reports commercial HBM4 shipments
entry.summary: Samsung says HBM4 mass production has begun and commercial products have shipped. This establishes a product milestone, not a verified industry-wide output rate; comparable shipment volumes and packaging throughput remain research gaps.

entry.title: AWS reports deployed accelerator supply and production workloads
entry.summary: Amazon reports 1.4 million Trainium2 chips landed across its fleet and more than 500,000 in the operational Rainier cluster. Rainier is a subset of the fleet, so these counts must not be added. The same release says Trainium3 is delivering production workloads.

entry.title: Marvell / Celestial AI · acquisition completed
entry.summary: Marvell completed the acquisition of Celestial AI. Its optical scale-up technology now belongs within the Marvell profile; acquisition value is not product revenue.

entry.title: Fiber supply also creates industrial work
entry.summary: Corning’s Meta agreement is for up to $6 billion over multiple years and supports a North Carolina expansion. Its employment language includes sustaining an existing workforce, not 5,000 newly created jobs.

entry.title: Micron announces New York groundbreaking; production expected in 2030
entry.summary: Micron announced the groundbreaking for its New York memory complex, with up to four fabs planned. The company expects production to start in 2030 and ramp through the decade. Its regional jobs projection is a long-term impact claim, not a count of workers already hired.

entry.title: Solar manufacturing delivers reported Louisiana employment
entry.summary: First Solar’s inauguration release reports a $1.1 billion Louisiana facility and more than 700 current employees. Manufacturing began in July 2025; the later staffing target and full-ramp module capacity remain distinct from that reported milestone.

entry.title: Another chapter in Wisconsin’s buildout
entry.summary: Microsoft announced an additional $4 billion commitment for a second Wisconsin data center over three years. The pledge is tracked separately from completed construction and actual expenditure.

entry.title: AlphaGenome supplies measured scientific prediction results
entry.summary: DeepMind reports gains on DNA-sequence and regulatory-variant prediction evaluations; its research page notes Nature publication in January 2026. These are research prediction outcomes, not evidence of new treatments or demonstrated clinical benefit.

entry.title: Broadcom Bailly CPO · volume production reported
entry.summary: Broadcom described its Tomahawk 5-Bailly CPO generation as in volume production while announcing a newer generation. That does not establish universal CPO adoption.

entry.title: Training capacity matters
entry.summary: IBEW’s May 2025 reporting describes rising data-center labor demand and a nearly tripled apprenticeship program at Baltimore Local 24. This is a dated local union account, not a national hiring statistic.

entry.title: Transformer investment links grid demand to manufacturing jobs
entry.summary: Eaton announced a $340 million Jonesville transformer manufacturing investment, with production and hiring for 700 local jobs expected to begin in 2027. The 2025 disclosure remains a plan until delivery evidence is reviewed.

entry.title: Power equipment expansion includes a U.S. workforce commitment
entry.summary: GE Vernova announced almost $600 million for U.S. factories and facilities over two years, with approximately 1,500 expected factory and engineering jobs. This is a dated investment and hiring plan; realized employment remains a follow-up question.

entry.title: Customer-support field evidence goes beyond adoption counts
entry.summary: The revised Generative AI at Work paper studies 5,172 support agents and reports a 15% average increase in issues resolved per hour, with heterogeneous effects. This is historical evidence from a particular workplace setting, not a 2026 economy-wide productivity estimate.

entry.title: An advanced manufacturing milestone
entry.summary: TSMC reports that its 2 nm technology entered high-volume manufacturing in the fourth quarter of 2025. Its annual report also describes expanding manufacturing capacity across regions.

entry.title: Useful model capability became more affordable
entry.summary: Stanford’s 2025 AI Index records a drop from $20 to $0.07 per million tokens at a GPT-3.5-equivalent benchmark threshold between November 2022 and October 2024.

entry.title: AI reaches more organizations
entry.summary: The 2026 AI Index reports organizational AI adoption of 88%, following 78% in the previous report. These survey results track use; measured business outcomes remain a separate research question.

entry.title: Veo 3 zero-shot video reasoning
entry.summary: Google DeepMind’s Veo 3 demonstrated zero-shot abilities to simulate physical behaviors like buoyancy and maze solving across more than 18,000 generated videos, indicating emergent video reasoning without task-specific training.

entry.title: Lumentum UHP laser accelerated life test
entry.summary: Lumentum reports an accelerated life-test program for its ultra-high-power laser platform used in ELSFP solutions for co-packaged optics. The company states more than 100 million accelerated device hours with zero observed failures and stable operating characteristics, supporting reliability objectives for large-scale AI and CPO deployments.

entry.title: Richland Parish Data Center · Mortenson scope
entry.summary: Mortenson lists its scope for the Richland Parish Data Center as site prep and grading, underground utilities, medium-voltage distribution and substations for onsite power, onsite water treatment, offsite wastewater treatment, administration and IBOS buildings and guard houses, and outside plant fiber distribution.

entry.title: Turner Construction selected for Meta Jeffersonville hyperscale data center
entry.summary: Turner Construction announced on January 25, 2024 that it was selected to build a hyperscale data center campus for Meta in Jeffersonville, Indiana. The company states the nearly 700,000-square-foot campus will represent an investment of more than $800 million and support approximately 100 jobs once completed.

entry.title: Isomorphic Labs Series B funding
entry.summary: Isomorphic Labs announced $2.1 billion Series B funding on 12 May 2026 to scale its AI drug design engine and advance therapeutic programs toward the clinic. The financing is led by Thrive Capital with participation from Alphabet, GV, MGX, Temasek, CapitalG and the UK Sovereign AI Fund.

entry.title: NVIDIA describes NVLink Fusion for custom XPUs
entry.summary: NVIDIA describes NVLink Fusion as a way to connect custom XPUs to its AI infrastructure. The company presents performance and time-to-market benefits for semi-custom AI factories; the article does not establish measured deployment gains. Correction: Classifies a company architecture announcement; avoids implying an initial launch or measured deployment gains.

entry.title: Amazon Nova Act SDK research preview
entry.summary: Amazon announced a research preview of the Amazon Nova Act SDK on nova.amazon.com, allowing developers to experiment with an early version of a model trained to perform actions within a web browser. Correction: Classifies research-preview availability as a company announcement rather than a measured research result.

entry.title: Nebius multi-billion dollar Microsoft AI infrastructure agreement
entry.summary: In its September 8, 2025 announcement, Nebius said it would deliver dedicated AI infrastructure capacity to Microsoft from its Vineland, New Jersey data center under a multi-year agreement, with delivery planned to begin later in 2025. This records the agreement, not subsequent commissioning. Correction: Classifies the agreement as a company announcement and limits the summary to the retained evidence; removes the 2026 growth statement.

entry.title: America’s Workforce Academy first cohort graduates
entry.summary: In its August 18, 2026 update, Meta reported that the first America’s Workforce Academy cohort had graduated the preceding week. Meta described a free program with credentials and guaranteed jobs, backed by an initial $115 million first-year investment. This is a company-reported milestone, not a verified placement count. Correction: Anchors relative timing to the source publication date and distinguishes a company announcement from verified job placements.

entry.title: Coding activity and shipped software are different outcomes
entry.summary: A matched event study of more than 100,000 GitHub developers estimates larger gains in commits than in software releases after AI-tool adoption. The authors identify review and integration as potential bottlenecks. These are observational estimates for the studied tools and users, not a universal productivity multiplier.

entry.title: METR flags limits in updated coding-productivity estimates
entry.summary: METR says selection effects and time measurement make its follow-up developer experiment an unreliable measure of current AI productivity. It considers improved speed plausible but the size uncertain. Its early-2025 slowdown finding remains a result for that earlier study, not a current universal effect.

entry.title: Agent use extends into analysis and document work
entry.summary: Anthropic analyzes roughly 400,000 Claude Code sessions and reports increasing use for analysis, prose and operating software. Its expertise and success measures rely on transcript classifiers and telemetry. The study supports broader-use investigation, but does not directly measure company productivity, worker earnings or net employment.

entry.title: Primary-care trial separates workflow assistance from patient outcomes
entry.summary: A cluster-randomized trial enrolled 9,691 patients at 16 Kenyan primary-care facilities during April–July 2025. LLM assistance did not significantly change the primary 14-day treatment-failure outcome. This study does not establish universal benefit, lack of benefit, or safety equivalence; the result applies to the studied workflow and follow-up period.

entry.title: Micron HBM4 high-volume production for NVIDIA Vera Rubin
entry.summary: Micron says it has begun volume shipment of HBM4 36GB 12H in the first quarter of calendar year 2026 and is designed for NVIDIA Vera Rubin. The company reports over 11 Gb/s pin speeds enabling bandwidth greater than 2.8 TB/s, representing a 2.3 times bandwidth and greater than 20% power efficiency improvement over its HBM3E.

entry.title: Fervo 3.0 well design drilling pace record at Cape Station Phase II
entry.summary: Fervo says it drilled Sawtooth 7, the ninth 3.0 well at Cape Station Phase II, from spud to total depth in 21 days, reaching 19,448 feet measured depth with a 7,500-foot lateral in a 460 degrees Fahrenheit resource. The company says this sets a new company record for drilling pace on its most complex well design to date.

entry.title: S+B Gruppe secures planning permission for 12MW NIMB data center in Bucharest
entry.summary: S+B Gruppe has secured planning permission to build a 12MW Tier III data center named NIMB in Bucharest’s northern office district, with 36,597 square feet of white space and an expected opening in 2028.

entry.title: Sunrun Voltus residential battery capacity for AI hyperscale data centers
entry.summary: Sunrun will supply Voltus with capacity from residential solar-plus-storage systems in PJM and MISO under an agreement supporting Voltus’ Bring Your Own Capacity programs for AI hyperscale data centers, announced August 17, 2026. The companies did not disclose the capacity, number of participating homes, or specific hyperscaler projects.

entry.title: AMD Instinct MI355X systems now live in Saudi Arabia
entry.summary: AMD says AMD Instinct MI355X GPU-based AI infrastructure built on Cisco Silicon One-based AI networking is now live in Saudi Arabia and serving HUMAIN customers in the Kingdom and beyond.

entry.title: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
entry.summary: Rule from Commerce Department, Industry and Security Bureau. Docket Docket No. 260710-0168. Published in the Federal Register 2026-07-14. https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/14/2026-14132/enhanced-favorable-treatment-for-the-united-arab-emirates-under-the-export-administration

entry.title: Zankore secures $3.1bn senior term loan for AI cloud build-out
entry.summary: Zankore has secured $3.1 billion in financing for the first phase of its AI cloud build-out. The joint venture targets an initial buildout of 100MW of Nvidia AI infrastructure in Indonesia, ultimately aiming to expand to 1GW.

entry.title: Nostrum Evergreen Data Center electrical authorization
entry.summary: Data Riocaya’s Nostrum Evergreen Data Center in Badajoz received preliminary administrative authorization for electrical infrastructure, including a 220-kV interconnection field and underground lines, with grid connection capacity up to 300MW for AI infrastructure.

entry.title: Oracle Q1 FY2027 GPU delivery and data center capacity
entry.summary: Oracle says it delivered more than 300,000 GPUs and 850MW of data center capacity to customers during Q1 of fiscal year 2027, revealed during the earnings call on September 10, 2026.

entry.title: Claude Opus 5 launch
entry.summary: Anthropic says Claude Opus 5 is available today, priced at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens, the same as Opus 4.8.

entry.title: Flex to acquire EPC Power for $4.4B
entry.summary: Flex says it will acquire EPC Power for $4.4 billion, adding 800V DC and grid-forming power-conversion technology to its data center infrastructure business. The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals and other closing conditions.

entry.title: SK hynix · HBM4
entry.summary: SK hynix announced on September 12, 2025 that it has completed development and finished preparation of HBM4 mass production for the world’s first time, positioning the product as a next generation memory for ultra-high performance AI.

entry.title: Lightmatter Passage CPO sampling with Qualcomm
entry.summary: Lightmatter announced on March 11, 2026 that it successfully sampled the Passage Co-Packaged Optics chiplet with Qualcomm Technologies, demonstrating 1.6 Tbps throughput per fiber using a 16-wavelength DWDM architecture at 112G per SerDes lane. The company says the integration provides up to 8X more bandwidth per fiber than existing Near-Packaged Optics and CPO solutions and is positioned for hyperscaler deployment.

entry.title: Meta Kuna Data Center online
entry.summary: Meta says the Kuna Data Center is online and operational, part of infrastructure that helps bring its technologies and programs to life. The project broke ground in 2022 and supported 1,600 skilled trade workers at peak construction with an investment of more than $1.2 billion in Kuna.

entry.title: AlphaGenome API preview launch
entry.summary: Google DeepMind says it is introducing AlphaGenome, a new AI tool that predicts how single variants or mutations in human DNA sequences impact biological processes regulating genes, and is making it available in preview via the AlphaGenome API for non-commercial research.

entry.title: Grok 4.6 release announcement
entry.summary: SpaceXAI says it is releasing Grok 4.6 today, building on Grok 4.5 with a focus on long-running agents and more ambitious interactive and visual work, and that it stays with complex tasks across many steps.

entry.title: Claude in Chrome generally available
entry.summary: Anthropic says Claude in Chrome is now generally available on every paid Claude plan, with autonomous browser actions validated by a safety classifier before execution.

entry.title: Grok 4.6 generally available on Amazon Bedrock
entry.summary: xAI says Grok 4.6 is now generally available on Amazon Bedrock, offering a 500k context window and configurable reasoning efforts (low, medium, high, xhigh). Pricing is listed as $2 per 1 million tokens input, $0.50 per 1 million tokens cached input, and $6 per 1 million tokens output.

entry.title: Grok 4.6 available via Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
entry.summary: xAI says Grok 4.6 is now available on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform via Model Garden, with a 500k context window and configurable reasoning efforts (low, medium, high, xhigh). Pricing is listed as $2 per 1 million tokens input, $0.50 per 1 million tokens cached input, and $6 per 1 million tokens output.

entry.title: Google DeepMind releases Gemini 3.8 Live models
entry.summary: Google DeepMind says it released new Gemini Live models in the Gemini API and Google AI Studio, including Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking for real-time voice-first product experiences.
